answer: The given system of equations is: \\ $x + 2y + z = 3$ \\ $x + y + z = \lambda$ \\ $3x + y + 3z = \lambda^2$ \\ \\ Write the augmented matrix $[A|B]$ and reduce it to row echelon form: \\ $\begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 & 1 & 3 \\ 1 & 1 & 1 & \lambda \\ 3 & 1 & 3 & \lambda^2 \end{pmatrix}$ \\ \\ Apply $R_2 \to R_2 - R_1$ and $R_3 \to R_3 - 3R_1$: \\ $\sim \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & -1 & 0 & \lambda - 3 \\ 0 & -5 & 0 & \lambda^2 - 9 \end{pmatrix}$ \\ \\ Apply $R_3 \to R_3 - 5R_2$: \\ $\sim \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & -1 & 0 & \lambda - 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & \lambda^2 - 9 - 5(\lambda - 3) \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & -1 & 0 & \lambda - 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & \lambda^2 - 5\lambda + 6 \end{pmatrix}$ \\ \\ For consistency, the last entry must be zero: $\lambda^2 - 5\lambda + 6 = 0 \implies (\lambda - 2)(\lambda - 3) = 0 \implies \lambda = 2$ or $\lambda = 3$. \\ \\ **Case 1: When $\lambda = 3$** \\ $-y = 0 \implies y = 0$. \\ From $x + 2y + z = 3 \implies x + z = 3$. Let $z = k$, then $x = 3 - k$. \\ Solution: $(3-k, 0, k)$ for any real $k$. \\ \\ **Case 2: When $\lambda = 2$** \\ $-y = 2 - 3 = -1 \implies y = 1$. \\ From $x + 2(1) + z = 3 \implies x + z = 1$. Let $z = c$, then $x = 1 - c$. \\ Solution: $(1-c, 1, c)$ for any real $c$.
proTip: For a system to be consistent, the rank of the coefficient matrix must equal the rank of the augmented matrix.
